task_2.title: Deprecate zope-interface validator support in attrs
task_2.description: Version 23.1.0 deprecates `attrs.validators.provides`, which was the library's built-in support for validating `zope-interface` providers. The validator remains available for now, but creating it now emits a deprecation warning so users can migrate away before the support is removed in a future release.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that applications upgrading from 22.2.0 to 23.1.0 treat `attrs.validators.provides` as deprecated `zope-interface` support: existing uses should still validate values as before, but use of the validator must surface a deprecation signal so consumers can migrate before removal.

expectation.grounded: In attrs 23.1.0, calling `attrs.validators.provides(interface)` must still return a validator for the requested interface, but the call is deprecated and must emit a `DeprecationWarning`. The returned validator should continue enforcing the existing interface-provision contract and continue raising `TypeError` for values that do not provide the required interface.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, code that relies on the `provides` validator should keep working for now, but the library should clearly warn that this `zope-interface` integration is deprecated and scheduled for removal. Users should be able to detect the deprecation at runtime without losing the current validation behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the validator's public entry point or its current success/failure semantics in this release. The deprecation signal must occur when `attrs.validators.provides(...)` is used, and invalid values must still fail through the validator's existing `TypeError` behavior rather than a different exception path.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should introduce a warning, not an immediate break. Existing consumers should see the new deprecation notice while all current pass/fail validation outcomes remain stable until the feature is actually removed.

behavior: Using `attrs.validators.provides(interface)` now emits a runtime `DeprecationWarning`.
The `provides` API remains available in 23.1.0 and still returns a validator object.
Values that satisfy the required interface continue to pass validation.
Values that do not provide the required interface continue to fail validation with `TypeError`.
acceptance_criteria: When application code creates a validator with `attrs.validators.provides(...)`, it should receive a `DeprecationWarning` indicating that the built-in `zope-interface` support is deprecated.
When a value provides the required interface, validation through the returned `provides` validator should still succeed as it did before the upgrade.
When a value does not provide the required interface, validation through the returned `provides` validator should still fail with `TypeError`.

Upgrading to 23.1.0 should not require immediate replacement of `attrs.validators.provides`, but continued use should be treated as temporary because the feature is slated for removal in a future release.

task_3.title: Support field-name strings in attrs filters
task_3.description: Upgrading to attrs 23.1.0 adds support for passing field names as strings to attrs filter helpers, so callers can include or exclude attrs fields by name without first retrieving Attribute objects, while preserving existing class-based and Attribute-based filtering behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 23.1.0 allows users to pass literal field-name strings to `attrs.filters.include()` and `attrs.filters.exclude()` when filtering attrs fields, while preserving existing behavior for class selectors and `attrs.Attribute` selectors.

expectation.grounded: `attrs.filters.include()` and `attrs.filters.exclude()` must accept selector arguments that are classes, field-name strings, or `attrs.Attribute` objects. The predicate returned by `include()` should treat a field as selected when the field value's class matches a supplied class, the field's `attribute.name` matches a supplied string, or the field matches a supplied `attrs.Attribute`. The predicate returned by `exclude()` should reject a field when any of those same selector kinds match.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to choose attrs fields by name in the same filtering APIs they already use for type-based or attribute-based selection. Name-based filtering should feel additive and consistent with the existing include/exclude behavior.

constraints.grounded: Existing selectors based on classes and `attrs.Attribute` objects must continue to behave as before. Mixed selector kinds must compose as alternative matching conditions. A string that does not exactly match the current field name must not independently alter the filter outcome.
constraints.conceptual: The new string input is a convenience extension, not a redesign. Existing filtering behavior must remain stable, and unknown field names should simply have no effect.

behavior: `attrs.filters.include(*what)` accepts field-name strings in addition to classes and `attrs.Attribute` objects.
`attrs.filters.exclude(*what)` accepts field-name strings in addition to classes and `attrs.Attribute` objects.
For `include()`, a field is retained when any supplied selector matches by value type, exact field name, or exact `attrs.Attribute`.
For `exclude()`, a field is omitted when any supplied selector matches by value type, exact field name, or exact `attrs.Attribute`.
Non-matching field-name strings do not change the result for unrelated fields.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller uses `attrs.filters.include()` with one or more field-name strings, fields whose names match those strings should be included even if no `attrs.Attribute` objects were supplied.
When a caller uses `attrs.filters.exclude()` with one or more field-name strings, fields whose names match those strings should be excluded even if no `attrs.Attribute` objects were supplied.
When field-name strings are combined with class selectors or `attrs.Attribute` selectors in either API, a match on any supplied selector should produce the expected include or exclude result.
When a supplied string does not match a field name, filtering behavior for other fields should remain unchanged apart from any other matching selectors.

task_1.title: Drop Python 3.6 support and deprecate legacy module metadata access
task_1.description: attrs 23.1.0 drops Python 3.6 support and moves packaging data to static package metadata. Existing consumers of legacy metadata attributes on the `attr` and `attrs` modules should still be able to read them for compatibility, but those lookups are now deprecated and backed by installed package metadata instead of hard-coded module globals.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 23.1.0 enforces Python 3.7+ support and preserves legacy packaging metadata access on `attr` and `attrs` in a backward-compatible but deprecated form.

expectation.grounded: The package should no longer support Python 3.6. The `attr` and `attrs` modules should continue exposing legacy metadata dunder attributes, including `__title__`, `__copyright__`, `__version__`, `__description__`, `__uri__`, `__url__`, `__author__`, `__email__`, and `__license__`, via module attribute lookup. Accessing those legacy metadata attributes should emit `DeprecationWarning`. `__version_info__` should still be available on both modules, return an `attr.VersionInfo` value derived from the installed package version, and not emit a deprecation warning. Requests for unsupported attribute names should raise `AttributeError`.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should require a supported Python runtime and keep old module metadata lookups working long enough for consumers to migrate to standard package metadata APIs. Deprecated metadata reads should still succeed with warnings, structured version info should remain available without warning, and invalid attribute access should continue to fail normally.

constraints.grounded: Do not reintroduce Python 3.6 compatibility. Keep legacy metadata behavior aligned between `attr` and `attrs`. Preserve normal `AttributeError` behavior for names outside the supported metadata set. Do not warn when `__version_info__` is accessed.
constraints.conceptual: Maintain compatibility for existing metadata consumers without silently accepting unsupported runtimes or masking invalid module attributes.

behavior: Python 3.6 is no longer a supported runtime for attrs 23.1.0.
Legacy packaging metadata is no longer stored as direct module globals and is instead resolved from installed package metadata when accessed.
Reading supported legacy metadata attributes on either `attr` or `attrs` continues to return the corresponding package metadata, but now emits `DeprecationWarning`.
`attr.__version_info__` and `attrs.__version_info__` continue to return a parsed `VersionInfo` object for the installed package version and do not emit a deprecation warning.
Accessing unsupported attribute names on `attr` or `attrs` raises `AttributeError`.
acceptance_criteria: When attrs 23.1.0 is used with Python 3.6, that runtime should be treated as unsupported.
Given an installed attrs 23.1.0 package, when a consumer reads `attr.__version__` or `attrs.__version__`, it should receive the installed package version and a `DeprecationWarning`.
When a consumer reads any other supported legacy metadata attribute on `attr` or `attrs`, it should receive the corresponding metadata value and a `DeprecationWarning`.
When a consumer reads `attr.__version_info__` or `attrs.__version_info__`, it should receive a `VersionInfo` object representing the installed version without a deprecation warning.
When a consumer requests an unsupported metadata-style attribute on `attr` or `attrs`, the module should raise `AttributeError`.

task_5.title: Allow frozen attrs exceptions to participate in normal traceback and chaining flows
task_5.description: Version 23.1.0 fixes a runtime bug in frozen attrs-based exception classes. Exceptions defined as frozen should now raise and propagate correctly when Python or surrounding frameworks update exception traceback or chaining metadata, instead of failing with a frozen-instance error.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that frozen attrs-based exception classes can be raised, propagated, and wrapped by normal Python exception-handling flows without failing when exception metadata is updated.

expectation.grounded: Instances of frozen attrs classes that are also BaseException subclasses, including exceptions created with attrs frozen APIs, should permit normal runtime assignment of exception metadata fields used by Python exception machinery: __traceback__, __cause__, and __context__. Raising such exceptions inside flows such as contextlib.contextmanager should preserve the original exception behavior instead of triggering FrozenInstanceError.
expectation.conceptual: Frozen exceptions should still behave like normal Python exceptions. When the runtime or a framework attaches traceback or chaining information during raise, re-raise, or wrapping, the exception should continue through that flow without being rejected for immutability.

constraints.grounded: Frozen behavior must remain unchanged for non-exception attrs instances and for attributes other than the standard exception metadata fields. Arbitrary attribute mutation on frozen instances should still be rejected with FrozenInstanceError.
constraints.conceptual: This fix must be narrowly scoped to exception bookkeeping. It should not weaken immutability for ordinary frozen objects or allow unrelated fields on frozen exceptions to become mutable.

behavior: Frozen attrs instances that subclass BaseException accept runtime updates to __traceback__.
Frozen attrs instances that subclass BaseException accept runtime updates to __cause__ and __context__ used for exception chaining.
Raising or propagating a frozen attrs-based exception through code that rewrites traceback metadata should surface the intended exception type rather than a FrozenInstanceError.
Attempts to set any other attribute on a frozen instance continue to fail with FrozenInstanceError.
acceptance_criteria: When a frozen attrs-defined exception is raised inside a context manager or other exception-handling wrapper that updates traceback information, it should propagate as that exception and not fail with FrozenInstanceError.
When Python sets exception chaining metadata on a frozen attrs-defined exception during exception propagation, the operation should succeed without breaking the raise flow.
When code attempts to assign a non-exception-metadata attribute on a frozen attrs instance, it should still be rejected as an immutability violation.

task_4.title: Generic attrs class introspection support
task_4.description: Upgrading to attrs 23.1.0 fixes introspection of parameterized generic attrs classes so the public helpers for detecting and retrieving attrs field metadata work on specialized generic aliases in the same way they already work on the generic base class.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that parameterized generic attrs classes are recognized and introspected consistently by the public attrs helpers, while non-attrs generic classes and invalid inputs continue to produce the existing unsupported-input behavior.

expectation.grounded: `attrs.has()` should return `True` for an attrs-decorated generic class and for its parameterized generic aliases, and should return `False` for non-attrs classes including parameterized generic aliases of non-decorated generic classes. `attrs.fields()` should accept a parameterized generic alias of an attrs-decorated generic class and return the same `attrs.Attribute` metadata tuple exposed by the generic base class. If a parameterized generic alias does not resolve to an attrs-decorated class, `attrs.fields()` should raise `attrs.exceptions.NotAnAttrsClassError`. If the input is neither a class nor a supported generic class alias, `attrs.fields()` should still raise `TypeError`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to pass a parameterized generic attrs class to the same introspection APIs they use for ordinary attrs classes. Those APIs should treat the parameterized generic as a valid attrs class, expose the same field metadata as the underlying generic definition, and continue to reject unsupported inputs through the established public behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not change existing behavior for non-generic callers. `attrs.has()` must remain a non-raising boolean check for unsupported classes. `attrs.fields()` must preserve its current return contract for valid attrs classes and continue to distinguish invalid non-class inputs from unsupported non-attrs classes via `TypeError` and `attrs.exceptions.NotAnAttrsClassError`, respectively.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should extend generic-class support without altering the current contract for existing valid or invalid inputs. Current callers should see the same results unless they are using parameterized generic attrs classes, which should now work.

behavior: `attrs.has()` now recognizes parameterized generic aliases of attrs-decorated generic classes as attrs classes.
`attrs.fields()` now accepts parameterized generic aliases of attrs-decorated generic classes and exposes their field metadata.
`attrs.has()` continues to return `False` for parameterized generic aliases whose base class is not attrs-decorated.
`attrs.fields()` raises `attrs.exceptions.NotAnAttrsClassError` for parameterized generic aliases whose base class is not attrs-decorated.
`attrs.fields()` still raises `TypeError` for inputs that are neither classes nor supported generic class aliases.
acceptance_criteria: When a user defines an attrs-decorated generic class and passes a parameterized form of that class to `attrs.has()`, it should return `True`.
When a user passes a parameterized form of an attrs-decorated generic class to `attrs.fields()`, it should return the same attribute names and metadata exposed by the generic base class.
When a user passes a parameterized form of a generic class that is not attrs-decorated to `attrs.has()`, it should return `False`.
When a user passes a parameterized form of a generic class that is not attrs-decorated to `attrs.fields()`, it should raise `attrs.exceptions.NotAnAttrsClassError`.
When a user passes an input that is not a class and not a supported generic class alias to `attrs.fields()`, it should raise `TypeError`.

task_8.title: Align attrs.asdict and attrs.astuple typing with AttrsInstance
task_8.description: The upgrade updates the public type signatures for attrs.asdict() and attrs.astuple() so they accept the attrs.AttrsInstance protocol instead of a generic untyped instance. This brings the attrs namespace into parity with the attr namespace and improves static typing for users working with attrs-based classes without changing documented runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 23.1.0 recognizes attrs-based instances passed to attrs.asdict() and attrs.astuple() as valid typed inputs, so users get consistent static typing across the attrs and attr namespaces.

expectation.grounded: The public type stubs for attrs.asdict() and attrs.astuple() should accept inputs typed as attrs.AttrsInstance rather than an unconstrained Any-like instance. Static type checking should therefore treat attrs instances as supported arguments for these two attrs namespace APIs, consistent with the corresponding attr namespace functions.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to call attrs.asdict() and attrs.astuple() on attrs-defined objects without losing type-checker support. The upgrade should make the typing contract for these conversion helpers consistent across equivalent public APIs.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable runtime semantics of attrs.asdict() or attrs.astuple(); the upgrade evidence supports a stub/signature refinement only. The accepted typed input should be described via attrs.AttrsInstance, and compatibility with existing attrs instances should be preserved.
constraints.conceptual: This change should improve type safety without altering how these functions behave at runtime. Existing supported attrs objects should continue to work the same way while type checkers become more precise.

behavior: attrs.asdict() is typed to accept attrs.AttrsInstance inputs.
attrs.astuple() is typed to accept attrs.AttrsInstance inputs.
The attrs namespace typing for these functions is aligned with the corresponding attr namespace APIs.
The upgrade affects static typing expectations rather than introducing a documented runtime behavior change.
acceptance_criteria: When a value is typed as attrs.AttrsInstance, calling attrs.asdict() on it should be accepted by the library's public typing contract.
When a value is typed as attrs.AttrsInstance, calling attrs.astuple() on it should be accepted by the library's public typing contract.
When users rely on the attrs namespace instead of the attr namespace, these two conversion helpers should expose equivalent input typing expectations.

Upgrading to 23.1.0 should not require users to expect new runtime validation, new runtime errors, or changed serialization behavior from attrs.asdict() or attrs.astuple() based on the documented evidence provided.

task_7.title: Restore backward-compatible unpickling for pre-22.2.0 attrs objects
task_7.description: attrs 23.1.0 restores compatibility for objects serialized before 22.2.0. Applications that persist or cache attrs instances with pickle should be able to load legacy data after upgrade without deserialization failures, while current pickle behavior continues to work.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 23.1.0 allows applications to unpickle previously persisted or cached attrs instances created by versions earlier than 22.2.0, so existing serialized data remains readable after upgrade.

expectation.grounded: attrs-generated `__setstate__` handling must accept both the current mapping-based pickle state and the legacy tuple-based pickle state used before 22.2.0. When legacy tuple state is encountered during unpickling, attribute values should be restored positionally to the instance instead of failing with attribute-related errors.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, old serialized attrs objects should load successfully even if they were created by older releases. The library should remain compatible with both old and current pickle formats, and deserialization should restore the object's data rather than breaking on legacy cached values.

constraints.grounded: Tuple-state support must be additive: dict-style state deserialization must continue to behave as before, and only values present in the serialized state should be applied during unpickling.
constraints.conceptual: The compatibility fix must not break deserialization of objects serialized by newer versions, and it must not invent or mutate state beyond what was actually stored.

behavior: Unpickling an attrs instance whose serialized state is a tuple must restore attributes by position rather than treating tuple entries as named fields.
Unpickling an attrs instance whose serialized state is a dict-like mapping must continue to restore attributes by name as in newer releases.
Applications that read legacy pickled attrs instances from persistence layers such as caches should no longer fail solely because those objects were serialized before 22.2.0.
acceptance_criteria: When an attrs instance serialized with a version earlier than 22.2.0 is unpickled under 23.1.0, it should deserialize successfully and preserve its stored attribute values.
When an attrs instance serialized with the newer mapping-based state format is unpickled under 23.1.0, it should continue to deserialize successfully.
When legacy serialized attrs data is loaded from an existing cache or other persistent store after upgrade, deserialization should not fail because the stored state uses the older tuple-based format.

task_6.title: Make @frozen PEP-681 aware for type checkers
task_6.description: The attrs 23.1.0 upgrade improves static typing for `@frozen` so PEP-681-aware type checkers, including pyright and mypy, recognize classes decorated with `@frozen` as frozen and reject instance attribute reassignment accordingly.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that classes declared with `@frozen` are treated as frozen by type checkers that implement PEP-681, so assigning to an instance attribute after construction is reported as an error instead of being accepted.

expectation.grounded: The public `attr.frozen`/`attrs.frozen` decorator should advertise frozen dataclass semantics to PEP-681-aware type checkers. This should apply to both direct decorator usage and called-decorator usage, while preserving the existing public decorator options. For classes created with `@frozen`, post-instantiation assignment to declared instance attributes should be rejected by compliant type checkers in the same way that frozen dataclass-style classes are rejected.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, `@frozen` should behave consistently across modern type checkers: a class marked as frozen should be understood as immutable for static analysis, and attempts to mutate its fields should be flagged as invalid.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to static typing behavior and should not alter runtime construction or mutation behavior beyond the existing runtime semantics of frozen attrs classes. `define`/mutable behavior should remain non-frozen by default, and `@frozen` should continue to support its established decorator forms and keyword options.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve checker understanding of frozen classes without changing how applications run or broadening immutability to APIs that are not declared frozen.

behavior: Classes decorated with `attr.frozen` or `attrs.frozen` are exposed to PEP-681 type checkers as frozen classes rather than ordinary mutable attrs classes.
Static reassignment of a declared instance attribute on a `@frozen` instance is reported as a type-checking error.
The frozen typing contract applies whether the decorator is used directly or invoked as `@frozen()` with configuration options.
The improvement aligns `@frozen` with the already-recognized frozen semantics expected by PEP-681-aware tooling, rather than requiring checker-specific special handling.
acceptance_criteria: When a user defines a class with `@frozen` and assigns to one of its instance attributes after creating an object, a PEP-681-compliant type checker should report that assignment as invalid.
When the same frozen class is declared using the called decorator form `@frozen(...)`, the type checker should still treat the instance fields as immutable.
When a class is declared with non-frozen attrs APIs, the upgrade should not cause it to be treated as frozen by default.
When users upgrade to attrs 23.1.0, pyright and mypy should agree that `@frozen` classes are frozen for static analysis.

task_9.title: Fix slotted attrs class closure updates without __code__ on Python 3.8+
task_9.description: Attrs 23.1.0 fixes a runtime compatibility bug in slotted class generation on Python 3.8 and newer. Slotted attrs classes now preserve closure-cell updates even in environments where function __code__ introspection is unavailable, preventing failures in compiled runtimes while preserving existing behavior on older Python versions.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that slotted attrs classes continue to work on Python 3.8 and newer even when function __code__ introspection is unavailable, and that methods relying on the class closure still observe the correct generated class.

expectation.grounded: For CPython 3.8+, slotted classes created through attrs APIs such as attrs.define must complete closure-cell updating without requiring function __code__ introspection. In those classes, methods that rely on the __class__ closure, including __attrs_post_init__ and zero-argument super(), should continue to resolve against the final generated class instead of failing because __code__ metadata is missing.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading to 23.1.0 should make slotted attrs classes reliable in modern Python runtimes, including compiled or restricted environments that do not expose normal function introspection. Class methods should keep behaving as if they were defined on the final class, with __class__ and super() continuing to work normally.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress existing slotted-class behavior in standard environments where __code__ is available. Preserve the existing compatibility behavior for Python versions earlier than 3.8 while ensuring the Python 3.8+ path no longer depends on __code__ introspection.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only remove the compatibility failure in newer Python environments and must not change established behavior for users who already rely on normal slotted attrs class semantics or older-version compatibility.

behavior: On Python 3.8 and newer, closure-cell updating for slotted attrs classes succeeds even if function objects do not expose a __code__ attribute.
Slotted attrs classes can still be constructed and instantiated in compiled or otherwise non-standard runtimes where introspection support is limited.
Methods on slotted attrs classes that capture __class__ observe the final generated class after attrs transforms the class.
Zero-argument super() in slotted attrs class methods such as __attrs_post_init__ continues to resolve and call parent implementations correctly.
Python versions earlier than 3.8 continue using the existing compatibility behavior for closure-cell updates.
acceptance_criteria: When a slotted class is defined with attrs on Python 3.8 or newer in an environment where function __code__ introspection is unavailable, creating and instantiating the class should succeed.
When a method on a slotted attrs class references __class__, it should resolve to the generated class rather than an outdated or missing class reference.
When a slotted attrs subclass uses zero-argument super() in __attrs_post_init__ or another method that captures __class__, it should invoke the parent implementation successfully.
When the same slotted attrs code runs in standard environments where function __code__ is available, its observable behavior should remain unchanged.
When running on Python versions earlier than 3.8, the existing closure-cell compatibility behavior should remain available.

task_11.title: Document pull request workflow expectations
task_11.description: The 23.1.0 update adds contributor-facing guidance for the pull request workflow, clarifying the expected checklist around tests, typing stubs, documentation updates, changelog fragments, and optional branch permissions. No runtime code changes are present in the provided diff.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that contributors upgrading to 23.1.0 have clear documentation of the expected pull request workflow and submission checklist, without changing the library's runtime behavior.

expectation.grounded: The contributor documentation should describe the pull request workflow expectations for changed code, including adding tests where applicable, updating Hypothesis strategies for new features, reflecting public API changes in type stubs and typing examples, updating documentation and version directives for changed public behavior, using semantic newlines in reStructuredText documentation, adding changelog news fragments, and considering maintainer push access to the pull request branch. The provided code diff shows no runtime API, exception, warning, or state-behavior changes.
expectation.conceptual: The release should improve contributor guidance by making the pull request process and required project maintenance tasks explicit. Upgrading to this version should not alter how the library behaves for end users at runtime.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce runtime-facing behavior changes, public API additions, modified exceptions or warnings, or other production code effects as part of this update; the supplied code diff is empty, so the change is documentation-only.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the change limited to contributor guidance. The library's observable runtime behavior must remain unchanged.

behavior: Contributor-facing documentation now defines the expected pull request workflow and checklist for project submissions.
The documented workflow explicitly covers maintenance expectations tied to changed code, public API typing updates, documentation updates, changelog entries, and related contribution hygiene.
No runtime behavior changes are evidenced in the provided code diff for this update.
acceptance_criteria: When a contributor reviews the project's contribution guidance for version 23.1.0, they should find explicit pull request workflow instructions and a submission checklist.
When a change affects public APIs, the documented checklist should state that corresponding type stub updates and typing examples are expected.
When a change affects documented behavior or introduces new public features, the documented checklist should state that contributor documentation and version metadata are expected to be updated.
When contributors prepare a pull request, the guidance should state that changelog news fragments are expected and that maintainers may be granted branch push access.
Upgrading from 22.2.0 to 23.1.0 should not change runtime behavior exposed to library consumers.

task_10.title: Preserve typing extras in attr.resolve_types
task_10.description: The attrs upgrade changes attr.resolve_types() so that, on Python 3.9 and newer, resolved field annotations keep typing extras such as Annotated metadata by default while still allowing callers to opt out and request the older stripped-type behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that applications using attr.resolve_types() can preserve typing extras during annotation resolution on supported Python versions, while still allowing callers to opt out when they need the pre-upgrade stripped-type behavior.

expectation.grounded: attr.resolve_types() should accept an include_extras keyword argument. On Python 3.9 and newer, it should pass include_extras through to typing.get_type_hints() and, by default, resolve attrs field types with typing extras preserved. When include_extras=False is supplied on those Python versions, resolved field types should omit extras and match the base hinted type. On older Python versions, type resolution should continue without relying on include_extras support.
expectation.conceptual: When attrs resolves annotations for a class, metadata-bearing type hints should be retained by default on runtimes that support them, so callers can observe the same enriched types they declared. Callers should also be able to request the legacy simplified result when they do not want typing extras preserved.

constraints.grounded: The change must remain scoped to attr.resolve_types() behavior and its resolved field types. Existing globalns, localns, and attribs inputs must continue to participate in type resolution. Python versions without typing.get_type_hints(include_extras=...) support must not fail because of the new argument.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should add extra-type preservation without regressing normal annotation resolution, forward-reference handling, or compatibility across supported Python versions.

behavior: attr.resolve_types() exposes a new include_extras parameter with a default value that enables extras preservation.
On Python 3.9 and newer, attr.resolve_types() preserves typing extras in resolved attrs field types by default.
On Python 3.9 and newer, passing include_extras=False causes resolved attrs field types to fall back to the underlying hinted type without typing extras.
On Python versions older than 3.9, attr.resolve_types() keeps resolving annotations without depending on include_extras support from typing.get_type_hints().
acceptance_criteria: When a class field uses a metadata-bearing annotation supported by typing extras and attr.resolve_types() is called on Python 3.9 or newer without overriding include_extras, the resolved attrs field type should retain that extra metadata.
When the same class is resolved on Python 3.9 or newer with include_extras=False, the resolved attrs field type should be the simplified underlying type rather than the metadata-bearing form.
When attr.resolve_types() is called with globalns, localns, or a subset of attribs, those inputs should continue to affect resolution as before.

When attr.resolve_types() is used on Python versions that do not support include_extras in typing.get_type_hints(), annotation resolution should still complete without introducing a version-specific failure from this new option.

task_12.title: Support type metadata in attrs.field() for dynamic class creation
task_12.description: attrs 23.1.0 adds a public type parameter to attrs.field() so dynamically generated classes built with attrs.make_class() can retain field type metadata at runtime. This makes wrapper and introspection-heavy usage more expressive without changing static type checker behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dynamically generated attrs classes can declare field type metadata directly in attrs.field() definitions used with attrs.make_class().

expectation.grounded: attrs.field() should accept an optional type parameter, and when that field object is used in attrs.make_class(), the resulting attrs attribute should expose the declared type through its runtime metadata. This addition is intended to support wrappers and runtime introspection; type checkers are not expected to consume type metadata passed through make_class().
expectation.conceptual: Users defining attrs classes dynamically should be able to attach a field's type at the point where they declare the field, and the generated class should preserve that type information for runtime inspection.

constraints.grounded: The new type parameter must be additive and optional. Existing attrs.field() calls without type must continue to work unchanged, and the added type metadata must not be treated as a new static typing guarantee for attrs.make_class()-generated classes.
constraints.conceptual: This should be a backward-compatible enhancement that preserves existing behavior while exposing declared types as runtime metadata only.

behavior: attrs.field() accepts an optional type argument as part of its public API.
When an attrs.field(type=...) definition is provided to attrs.make_class(), the generated class stores that declared type in the field's runtime metadata.
Dynamic class creation using attrs.field() without a type argument continues to behave as before.
The new type metadata is available for wrappers and runtime introspection, but it does not change type checker understanding of classes created with attrs.make_class().
acceptance_criteria: When a user passes attrs.field(type=SomeType) in the attribute mapping for attrs.make_class(), the resulting class should expose SomeType as that field's runtime type metadata.
When a user creates a dynamic attrs class with attrs.field() and does not supply type, the class should still be created with unchanged behavior.
When a user supplies type through attrs.field() for use with attrs.make_class(), the parameter should be accepted as part of the supported public API.

When users inspect dynamically created attrs fields at runtime, declared types supplied through attrs.field(type=...) should be preserved even though static type checkers do not rely on that metadata.

task_13.title: Adopt positional-instance usage for attrs evolve
task_13.description: Upgrading to attrs 23.1.0 changes the calling contract of attr.evolve() and attrs.evolve(): the source instance should be passed positionally, which now allows an attribute named inst to be updated normally. Passing the source instance through inst= remains temporarily supported for compatibility, but it now emits a deprecation warning and is scheduled for removal.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attr.evolve() and attrs.evolve() are used with the source instance as a positional argument so objects with a field named inst can be evolved correctly, while avoiding deprecated keyword-based instance passing that now warns and will later stop working.

expectation.grounded: In attrs 23.1.0, attr.evolve() and attrs.evolve() accept exactly one positional source instance and apply keyword arguments as field changes. When the source instance is passed positionally, a field named inst must be handled like any other updatable field. For compatibility, using inst= to provide the source instance still works but emits DeprecationWarning. Calling evolve without a source instance, or with more than one positional argument, raises TypeError.
expectation.conceptual: Evolving an attrs object should take the original object as the first argument, and every legitimate field, including one named inst, should remain updateable. Older keyword-based instance passing should still function temporarily with a deprecation warning, while malformed calls should fail with normal argument errors.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing copy-with-changes semantics for valid attrs instances that already pass the source object positionally. Keep normal attrs class validation and field-update behavior intact. Limit the new warning behavior to the compatibility path where inst= is used to supply the source instance.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should preserve existing correct evolve behavior and only alter the API contract around how the original object is supplied. Backward compatibility should remain temporary rather than silently changing results for existing callers.

behavior: Passing the source instance as the sole positional argument allows attr.evolve() and attrs.evolve() to update an attribute named inst through keyword changes.
Passing the source instance with inst= continues to produce an evolved object for now, but emits DeprecationWarning at runtime.
Calling attr.evolve() or attrs.evolve() without supplying a source instance raises TypeError.
Calling attr.evolve() or attrs.evolve() with more than one positional argument raises TypeError.
acceptance_criteria: When an attrs instance is evolved using the instance as the first positional argument and a changed value for a field named inst, it should return a new instance reflecting the updated inst field.
When attr.evolve() or attrs.evolve() is called with inst= used as the source instance, it should still perform the evolve operation but surface a DeprecationWarning.
When attr.evolve() or attrs.evolve() is called without any source instance, it should fail with TypeError.
When attr.evolve() or attrs.evolve() is called with multiple positional arguments, it should fail with TypeError.

task_14.title: Support tuple validators in attrs.validators.optional
task_14.description: The upgrade expands `attrs.validators.optional()` so callers can pass a tuple of validators anywhere a single validator or list of validators was previously accepted. Optional attributes should continue to allow `None`, while non-`None` values are validated against all validators supplied in the tuple.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `attrs.validators.optional()` accepts validator tuples as a supported input form, so optional attributes can be declared with multiple validators using either a list or a tuple while preserving the existing behavior that `None` is allowed and non-`None` values are validated.

expectation.grounded: `attrs.validators.optional()` must accept a callable validator, a list of validator callables, or a tuple of validator callables. When given a tuple, it must behave like the existing list form: `None` remains valid, and any non-`None` value is checked by all validators contained in the tuple through the same combined-validation behavior already used for lists.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to define optional validation with either one validator or multiple validators supplied as a list or tuple. The optional wrapper should still permit `None`, and any real value should satisfy every validator that was provided.

constraints.grounded: Existing `optional()` behavior for single validators and lists must remain unchanged. The change is limited to recognizing tuples as another supported validators container and must not alter the rule that validation is skipped for `None` values but enforced for non-`None` values.
constraints.conceptual: The update should extend accepted input shapes without changing established optional-validation behavior. Existing usages must keep working the same way, and only the newly supported tuple form should be added.

behavior: `attrs.validators.optional()` accepts a tuple of validators in addition to a single validator or a list of validators.
When the wrapped attribute value is `None`, the optional validator treats it as valid without applying the nested validators.

When the wrapped attribute value is not `None` and the optional validator was created from a tuple, every validator in that tuple is applied using the same combined semantics as the existing list-based form.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller constructs `attrs.validators.optional()` with a tuple containing one or more validators, it should create a usable optional validator instead of rejecting that input form.
When an attribute using `attrs.validators.optional((...))` is assigned `None`, it should be accepted the same way as other `optional()` validators.

When an attribute using `attrs.validators.optional((...))` is assigned a non-`None` value, it should be validated against all validators in the tuple with the same pass/fail outcome as if the same validators had been supplied in a list.
When existing code uses `attrs.validators.optional()` with a single validator or a list of validators, its observable validation behavior should remain unchanged after the upgrade.
